children: A federal judge in Texas has been temporarily suspended from hearing cases after a judicial investigation determined she likely suffers from a mental condition interfering with her ability to perform the responsibilities of her office.
The 5th Circuit Judicial Council in an

that was made public on Monday said a judicial inquiry found that US District Judge Ada Brown in Dallas had "abandoned her post as a federal judge" while stepping aside from numerous cases and inundating court staff and judges with "bizarre emails" and "racial insults."

Judicial misconduct investigations are typically conducted confidentially. But the judicial council on Monday voted to make much of it public after Brown on Saturday "widely disseminated confidential materials related to these proceedings."

Bloomberg Law on Saturday published a report citing internal 5th Circuit records regarding the investigation into Brown, who was appointed to the US District Court for the Northern District of Texas by President Donald Trump during his first term.

A day earlier, a three-judge investigative committee had ordered Brown to sit for an interview on October 30 to address a judicial misconduct complaint that was initiated against her by Chief US Circuit Judge Jennifer Walker Elrod.
Brown could not be reached for comment by Reuters on Monday.

The judicial misconduct proceedings began after someone filed a complaint alleging Brown had made inappropriate and hostile comments toward that person and may be suffering from a mental condition interfering with her duties.

Elrod in August appointed a special committee that included herself to investigate the matter. The committee determined there was a reasonable basis to conclude she was suffering from such a mental health issue.

The committee pointed to instances in which Brown made "aberrant and inappropriate comments" during a hearing; requested the Texas Rangers investigate unsubstantiated claims that others were entering orders in her cases; and made "racial insults to judges and court staff."

Brown, who is Black and has Native American ancestry, also made claims that judges, attorneys and court staff "are discriminating and retaliating against her because of her race and/or gender," according to a 5th Circuit order.
The investigation also found she had recused herself from 40 cases since June for unexplained or unusual reasons, such as by citing concerns about the "constitutionality and ethics of these matters."

The inquiry found that a significant backlog of outstanding matters had developed on her docket, with the judge for years habitually delaying rulings on motions, which the order described as a "dereliction" of her duties.

Based on those allegations, the committee on September 21 ordered Brown to sit for a psychiatric exam, and the judicial council on September 29 ordered her cases to be reassigned temporarily and that no further cases be assigned to her.

Documents released by the 5th Circuit said Brown in response to the inquiry had failed to respond to numerous questions. At one point she said she planned to resign, though she has not done so even while refusing to return to work, according to the 5th Circuit documents.
